name: TX-25
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Williams running with large financial advantage
No polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Republican Roger Williams: an R+11 district, incumbency, and a roughly $1.4 million warhead against an underfunded challenger. Markets price the race around 95% Republican, and with no polling to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays close to the baseline.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a Democratic surge or a major scandal involving Williams could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-25 is a heavily Republican district in central Texas, where incumbent Roger Williams is seeking another term against Democrat Dione Sims. The seat has a strong Republican partisan lean, and Williams enters the general election with a substantial fundraising edge, holding over $1 million in cash. No public polling of the race is available, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 5% chance of an upset. The forecast expects Williams to win by roughly 15 points, with uncertainty reflecting the absence of polling. The race is rated Likely Republican.
